learningObjective: Reason about the trade-off between compilation-time budget and end-to-end wall-clock savings across serving scenarios.

canonicalClaims.claim: The value of a longer tuning budget depends on the ratio of compilation cost to summed serving cost; heavily-served models amortize longer tuning easily, while short-lived experiments do not. Recompilation on shape or config changes is a hidden compile-budget line item.
conditions: The serving workload's request count and lifetime are estimated.
Recompilation guards and their frequencies are known.
nonImplications: Does not imply longer tuning always yields runtime speedup — cost-model plateaus and noise cap gains.
Does not imply short tuning is always sufficient.

misconceptions.claim: Tuning budget is orthogonal to serving latency; once the artifact is compiled, tuning does not affect performance.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tuning selects the schedule that determines the compiled artifact's runtime; more tuning budget can find a faster schedule.

misconceptions.claim: 10× more tuning trials yield 10× runtime speedup.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tuning curves show diminishing returns; late trials contribute much less than early ones.

misconceptions.claim: Recompilation cost is negligible because it happens only once per program run.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Under `torch.compile` with shape variance, recompilation can happen many times per program run, one per unique shape combination.

misconceptions.claim: For any serving workload, spending more compile time is always worthwhile.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For short-lived / one-off experiments, extra compile time dwarfs runtime savings.

implementationFacts: TorchInductor exposes `TORCH_LOGS=+recompiles` to surface recompilation events.
performanceScenarios: Serving 10M requests/day: 4-hour extra tuning that saves 5 ms/request pays back within 1 day.
One-off experiment: 4-hour tuning saves 5 ms — net loss.
